newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK ISLAMIST PM SEES $29 BILLION SELL-OFF INCOME.
newsitem.headline: TURK ISLAMIST PM SEES $29 BILLION SELL-OFF INCOME.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told members of his party on Tuesday the state would raise revenues of $29 billion from privatisation during the year.
The ambitious forecast compares with predictions by privatisation officials that 1997 sell-off income will amount to $5 billion.
"Additional revenues of $29 billion will go to the state in one year from privatisation," Erbakan told a meeting of his Welfare Party in parliament.
"The most open proof of this is the $891 million of actual privatisation in two months from the hands of the OIB (Privatisation Administration) alone," he said.
Turkey's ten-year-old privatisation programme has stalled repeatedly in the face of legal and parliamentary challenges, which have held revenues down to just $3 billion until this year.
The programme has since been boosted by the sale of three small banks and a green light from the constitutional court to sell Turk Telekom, the telecommunications company.
However, doubt has been cast on demand for future sell-offs in the light of limited interest in the steelmaker Erdemir.

Erbakan's forecast included OIB privatisation revenues of $5 billion and $1 billion from the first tranche of Turk Telekom, along with $2 billion from the sale of finance ministry land and property $2 billion from the renting of power stations.
